audits.title: AgentRewind: Recoverable Execution for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
verified: The primary arXiv text defines aligned recoverable checkpoints d_t=(c_t,s_t) and restores both recorded agent context and controlled environment state before resuming with rewind memory.

The controlled environment recovery boundary is the workspace directory tree. The paper explicitly states that network requests, external-service calls and external runtime state outside that workspace cannot be undone by rewind.
MettleBench contains 82 tasks. The primary Table 1 reports GPT-5.4 Continue success 62.2% under mini-SWE-agent.
not_primary_bound_in_this_run: The worker's Restart-with-Experiences 78.0%, AgentRewind 87.8%, and component ablations 43.9/65.9/51.2 were visible through a detailed public extraction, but the exact primary-table cells were not directly exposed by the primary arXiv transport used in this invocation. They therefore remain secondary-extracted rather than upgraded to primary-verified here.
audits.scope: Supports the architectural claim that useful rewind must coordinate reasoning/context and controlled mutable world state, while local rewind does not reverse external effects. Does not establish rollback of remote effects, payment/message undo, or autonomous trigger reliability.

audits.title: ACRFence: Preventing Semantic Rollback Attacks in Agent Checkpoint-Restore
verified: The primary paper's testbed uses Claude Code CLI backed by Qwen3-32B, with simulated MCP bank/cloud/approval services and checkpoints placed after verification but before the irreversible action.

Action Replay: all 10 checkpoint-restore trials produced duplicate irreversible commits (10/10), while the no-checkpoint baseline produced none (0/10). The paper attributes the duplicate to the restored LLM regenerating a fresh request identity that bypasses duplicate detection.
Authority Resurrection: stateless single-use-token validation allowed all reuse attempts (2/2), while stateful server-side consumption/revocation rejected the reuse attempts.

The proposed ACRFence mitigation records irreversible effects and applies semantic replay-or-fork logic at the tool boundary, but the paper explicitly states that ACRFence itself is not yet implemented/evaluated and that the analyzer LLM's accuracy, overhead and evasion surface remain future work.
audits.scope: This directly supports the failure mechanism that syntactic idempotency keys can be insufficient across checkpoint restore for nondeterministic LLM callers. It does not establish production incident prevalence, a general 100% attack rate, or effectiveness of ACRFence itself.

combined_implication: The two primary sources are complementary: AgentRewind explicitly bounds what local checkpoint restore can undo, while ACRFence shows a proof-of-concept in which post-restore LLM re-synthesis causes irreversible external effects or authority to repeat despite ordinary retry assumptions. Downstream recovery designs should therefore separate local context/world rollback from durable external-effect identity and authority-consumption state.
